additions.site_identity_review: Digital Realty states on 27 August 2026 that ZUR4 expands its Glattbrugg campus 'comprising ZUR1, ZUR2, and ZUR3'. The existing Atlas site vcc-site-7a8c1ea8c8e33e9b29b6 (Digital Realty Zurich Glattbrugg Campus) was created for ZUR4 from the same release and is located at the official GWR entrance-address point of ZUR2 (Bäulerwisenstrasse 4); its ZUR4 addition explicitly recorded ZUR1-ZUR3 as operating campus buildings that were not admitted. Digital Realty's facility pages place ZUR1 at Sägereistrasse 35 Building 1, ZUR2 at Bäulerwisenstrasse 4 and ZUR3 at Bäulerwisenstrasse 6 / Sägereistrasse 35 Building 2, 8152 Glattbrugg, with facility points 106.2 m, 47.1 m and 35.8 m from the campus point. The three existing buildings are therefore one new project on the existing campus site, distinct from the ZUR4 construction project.

status.summary: Digital Realty's press release of 27 August 2026 announcing the start of construction of ZUR4 in Glattbrugg states that ZUR4 is planned to expand 'the already best-connected data center campus in Switzerland, comprising ZUR1, ZUR2, and ZUR3', that ZUR2 has been awarded the first SDEA PLATINUM Plus certification, and that with ZUR4 and the continued expansion of the Glattbrugg campus the company is creating an ecosystem that 'connects more than 200 customers on-site'. This present-tense description supports existing data-centre operations of ZUR1, ZUR2 and ZUR3 as of the release date. 27 August 2026 is the release date, not an opening date or inspection day; the buildings' original opening dates, IT capacity, floor area and utilisation are not stated, the 200-plus customers are a campus-wide figure, and ZUR4 (the separate existing project under construction) is not included.

locator.identity_review: This reuses the existing campus point unchanged: the official GWR entrance-address point of the ZUR2 building (EGID 210221229, Bäulerwisenstrasse 4), with its pinned evidence and unchanged uncertainty. ZUR2 is one of the three buildings of this project; Digital Realty's own facility points for ZUR1, ZUR2 and ZUR3 lie 106.2 m, 47.1 m and 35.8 m from it (geodesic, WGS84, pyproj). The point locates the campus and the ZUR2 entrance, not ZUR1 or ZUR3 individually or any building outline. The baseline ZUR4 project has no geometry-identity evidence, so none is pinned.

status.summary: FlexBase's media release of 1 September 2026 reports that the extensive excavation for the Technologiezentrum Laufenburg has been completed (over 480,000 m3 of earth and gravel moved), that over 98 percent of the roughly 1.4 m thick base slab area is compacted and concreted, and that with the start of the superstructure works the building now grows upward. The Technologiezentrum Laufenburg was therefore under construction on 1 September 2026, the release date. The status keeps the existing scope (the new FlexBase technology-centre building in Laufenburg); it does not assert completion, the operation of the planned AI data centre or of the redox-flow battery, or any capacity.

status_updates.identity_review: The release is FlexBase Group's own account of its Technologiezentrum Laufenburg construction site, built by ERNE-Gruppe, which is the existing Atlas record curated:flexbase-technologiezentrum-laufenburg-campus:new-technology-centre-current-build (FlexBase New Technology Centre Current Build), whose current 18 June 2026 status comes from ERNE-Gruppe's dated excavation and foundation update for the same 'Neubau FlexBase Technologiezentrum Laufenburg' project. FlexBase builds a single technology centre in Laufenburg (the AI data centre, battery storage and campus are parts of it); nothing in the release indicates another site, so this refreshes the same project with the same scope and leaves the campus locator unchanged.

status.summary: The Boletín Oficial de Aragón of 27 October 2026 publishes the Servicio Provincial de Zaragoza notice (signed 13 October) opening public information on Microsoft 7724 Spain, SL's application for a 132 kV underground line from the Puerto Venecia switching station to the SET Campus Microsoft 132/33 kV substation, whose purpose is to supply Microsoft's new data centre to be located in Zaragoza. A companion notice of 21 October 2026 covers the Puerto Venecia switching station itself on parcels 55 and 75 of polygon 88 (Plana de Torrero). This dated government record keeps the campus announced; it establishes no authorisation of the data centre, no building permit and no physical work.

status_updates.identity_review: Same campus as the existing imported record "Microsoft Zaragoza (Puerto Venecia) datacenter campus": the promoter is Microsoft 7724 Spain, SL, the company to which the Government of Aragón attributed the "Nuevo campus de centros de datos Microsoft" in the municipality of Zaragoza (declaration of 28 February 2025, recalled in Orden VFL/1410/2026); Microsoft's other two Aragón campuses are in La Muela and Villamayor de Gállego, so the "nuevo centro de datos a ubicar en Zaragoza" can only be this campus. The supply works are named after Puerto Venecia, and the Catastro reference point of polygon 88 parcel 55 (Plana de Torrero), where the SET Campus Microsoft line runs, is 0.85 km from the record's Puerto Venecia point. The refresh keeps the campus scope and the existing approximate locator; the nearest other Atlas sites are AWS La Cartuja (7.9 km) and ACS La Puebla (11.9 km). No queue fragment or claim touches this key.
